objectiveGates: Ratings 0, 1, 2 are permanently rejected forever. Never present these underlying physical works again in any future aesthetic review, regardless of filenames, photos or crop variants.
Rating 3 is solely a research deficit signal. Never present it to the user for re-review or selection. Find distinct better artworks for the affected subject.
Rating 4 is the ONLY scored tier awaiting explicit user decision. Show all past relevant 4-rated artworks for that decision, including when the same subject already has a different artwork rated 5.

Rating 5 is automatically confirmed and selected aesthetically. Include in the approved list; no further aesthetic confirmation. Original ownership, accurate identity and image rights still require technical checks.
Eligible, genuinely distinct, previously unscored new or historic paintings can be shown for the user's first score after image-quality/object-identity screening.
Subjects with no >=4 solo portrait need more research. A category with 4 but no 5 is user-decision pending, not a confirmed selection.
A Commons category file is not a physical painting and does not count until medium and depiction are established.
Collapse alternate images of one museum accession, enforce historical original-level rejection, and compare against the full historic 277-score corpus.
Never combine Philip Apostle with Philip Neri or similarly named saints; distinguish narrative scenes from solo-portrait coverage.
When a gallery is ready, deliver downloadable HTML directly in chat instead of only a repository link.

ratingDecisionSemantics.scope: All sacred-art user aesthetic ratings across previous and future review rounds

score0to2.rule: Immediately and permanently exclude from aesthetic gallery, re-review, shortlist, new candidate counts and final selections. Retain historical source/rating for audit only. New crop, resized source, file rename or photo is not a new work and cannot evade the rejection.

score3.rule: Insufficient; do not show for user re-rating or final selection. Use only internally to identify subject requiring further research, and source stronger distinct works. Preserve prior rating as evidence.

score4.rule: Present for the user's selection/confirmation review, even if another painting of the same subject has already been confirmed 5. Preserve 4 until explicitly changed; never automatically confirm, reject or suppress.

score5.rule: Automatically retain and select as aesthetically approved, no more aesthetic confirmation required. Technical identity, accurate depiction, reproducibility, licence and production checks remain separate.

nullRating.rule: Present only if a genuinely appropriate new candidate or previously proposed unscored painting and the source/image-quality gates pass; never infer approval.

ratingDecisionSemantics.categoryResearchRule: A subject/category with no qualifying subject-specific portrait scored 4 or 5 needs more paintings researched. A 4 removes the urgent research gap but is still awaiting user review; a 5 confirms a selection. Prior strong narrative scenes do not fulfill solo portrait coverage.
ratingDecisionSemantics.galleryRule: Display 4-rated works requiring the user's decision and eligible unrated new/prior proposals; 5-rated works in already-confirmed selected section. Never show 0-3 rated works as options again, not even greyed out, side-by-side or 'previously seen'.
ratingDecisionSemantics.originalIdentityRule: A rating belongs to the underlying original work. Copies, cropped photos, editions, and alternate files must not recreate rejected works as fresh candidates. Distinct physical originals only when their identifiers/provenance are established.
ratingDecisionSemantics.auditRule: Preserve all prior 0-5 data in non-UI historical ledger; do not delete or overwrite ratings to implement filter.
ratingDecisionSemantics.confirmedVsRights: 5 automatically means aesthetic selection, not automatic commercial-use rights or publication.
